title: Native sequence-site open tensor datum existence
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell, schemes X and Z in universe u, and an open immersion j:X -> Z. On the ringed sequence sites, with the positive-quotient coefficient sheaves and actual VaryingRing extension, pullback, native adjunction and sectionPull of [def-coef-native-open-tensor-evaluation-data], there exists an ordinary/cochain datum of [def-sf-open-tensor-cochain-data], namely NativeOpenTensorPrimitives.SystemOpenCochainsData l E j of [def-coef-native-open-tensor-primitives]. No datum at finite stages is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, separating the sequence-site and finite coefficient constructions.

proof.text: Construct the finite-limit-preserving inverse image of sheaves of sets on the vertical sequence sites. Lift it to modules and compose with scalar extension. The normalized module adjunction and uniqueness of left adjoints identify this functor with the actual native pull. Transport the ordinary tensorator along this isomorphism. Apply unit naturality to the sheaf of pairs of sections and the pure-tensor map; the normalized transpose formula identifies its scalar insertion with the specified native pullSection. This proves simultaneous naturality and the required pure-section equation, with all horizontal coefficient arrows retained.

Apply ringed-topos preservation of flat-term K-flat complexes to the constructed inverse image/scalar-extension functor. Transport K-flatness along its cochain isomorphism with native pull and flatness along the component isomorphisms. Take native push as right, with moduleAdj.

The native open-extension unit is invertible. Ordinary tensor support makes the extension counit at the ambient tensor invertible. Form the natural transformation which tensors this unit with the identity and composes with the inverse restriction tensorator. Transpose it under moduleJAdj. Its adjunct is an isomorphism; since its target is supported, the transpose is extension of its adjunct followed by the invertible counit, hence is invertible. Invert the resulting natural isomorphism to obtain ordinary; the Hom-equivalence inverse law gives ordinaryInverse, and naturality gives ordinaryNaturality.

Apply the direct-sum totalization comparisonFromComponents_exists to the inverse ordinary isomorphisms and their simultaneous naturality. Extension preserves all required coproducts as a left adjoint. Invert this cochain comparison. Its insertion formula gives summand after canceling its degreewise isomorphism; its naturality gives chainNaturality by the inverse-square identity. Assemble these fields into the unchanged native sequence-site cochain datum.
